title: Entropy-aware KV-affinity mini-batcher for low-jitter streaming chat
creator: Carlos Rivera
description: Design and implement a compact, entropy-aware micro-batcher for streaming chat completions that prioritizes KV-cache locality and GPU footprint minimization. The goal is to reduce tail latency and memory pressure for live streaming workloads with high session churn while preserving per-session low jitter and streaming token throughput.
acceptance_criteria: New mini-batcher reduces 95th percentile token latency by >= 15% on p50-p99 workloads vs current slab-batcher baseline
GPU memory fragmentation metric (per-GPU free-slab-runs) improves by >= 20% under the synthetic churn test
No regressions in per-session token order or stream interleaving; passes end-to-end integrity tests
Feature gated and rolloutable with runtime flag; end-to-end benchmark dashboard added to /dashboards/runtime/entropy-batcher

progress: 2026-02-18: Spike completed — small prototype that buckets requests by simple session hash and KV prefix achieved 8% p95 improvement on microbench
2026-02-25: Design doc v0 posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/team/runtime/entropy-batcher (link) — includes KV-affinity heuristic and entropy estimator math

2026-03-02: Implemented KV-affinity score (proto). Formula: affinity = w1 * prefix_overlap + w2 * recency_score - w3 * estimated_entropy; weights are configurable. Added unit tests for score semantics.
2026-03-05: Added microbatch packing window with preemption budget (default 8ms, budget 2ms). Early results show reduced per-token variance for sessions with long KV chains.
2026-03-09: Integrated slab-compaction hint into allocator; allocator will mark microbatch allocations as coalescible which triggers lightweight compaction at safe points.
2026-03-12: Running cluster-wide synthetic churn tests; observed 18% improvement p95 and ~22% fewer small free-slab runs on test GPUs. Preparing PR and benchmark dashboard.
design_notes: Rationale: current slab/continuous-batcher pairs create fragmentation when many short sessions allocate small KV pages. Grouping by KV-affinity reduces duplicate KV loads and improves cache hotness.

Entropy estimator: we sample token distribution for first N tokens of a request and compute a lightweight Shannon proxy; high estimated entropy -> avoid coalescing to preserve latency for exploratory queries.
Preemption window: microbatch waits up to W ms to collect affinity-aligned requests; if preemption budget exceeded, batch is flushed to maintain streaming SLOs.
Affinity score ties into routing: requests with high KV-affinity can be prioritized for packing; fallback when affinity low is to route to low-latency slab pool.
GPU allocation: implement 'coalescible' allocations tag so allocator can try to place coalescible KV slots contiguously to reduce fragmentation and improve memcpy locality during KV prefetch.
Trade-offs: slightly increased scheduling complexity and added per-request CPU work for scoring; mitigated by sampling and early bailout for trivial sessions.
Open question: best default entropy sampling depth (4 vs 8 tokens) — affects accuracy vs CPU cost. We'll A/B test on production traffic sample.
experiments_and_results: Experiment 1 (2026-02-20): simple session-hash grouping vs baseline slab-batcher. Dataset: 50k streaming sessions with median length 120 tokens. Result: p95 token latency down 8%, but increased p99 for <1% sessions due to mispacking.
Experiment 2 (2026-03-06): KV-affinity + entropy gating + 8ms microbatch window. Result: p95 down 18%, p99 down 7%, slab fragmentation metric improved 22%.
CPU overhead: affinity scoring adds ~0.6us/request average when sampling depth 4; negligible at current qps but accounted for in cost model.
Memory trade: slight temporary increase in per-GPU resident KV prefetch buffers while coalescing occurs, but net memory usage decreased due to fewer duplicate KV pages.
